name: Neon Blue
lede: Neon Blue is a vivid, electric blue whose earliest record in our data is not the modern word *neon* at all but a butterfly's wing in Werner's 1821 Nomenclature of Colours.

sections.title: Older than the word neon
sections.body:
Our library's earliest source for a color this close to #4666FF is Patrick Syme's 1821 edition of Werner's Nomenclature of Colours, where it is illustrated by the upper side of the wings of the small blue heath butterfly, the flower borage, and azure stone or lapis lazuli [1]. The modifier *neon*, by contrast, is a 20th-century word, and the xkcd crowd survey only recorded this exact name in 2010 [1]. ISCC-NBS lists it as a brilliant greenish blue in their 1955 charts, and the German RAL standard carries a close blue, RAL 5002, from 1927 [1].

At hex #4666FF it measures lightness 50 and chroma 89 in LCH, one of the most saturated blues in the library [1]. Its nearest named neighbors are [[bright-blue|Bright Blue]], 3.9 CIEDE2000 units off and read as almost the same color, and [[royal-blue|Royal blue]], 4.2 units off and duller; [[electric-blue|Electric Blue]] sits 6.5 units off, more vivid and darker [2]. The library separately logs Ultramarine Blue as a near-duplicate across five different sources [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive has a blue this vivid covering even 1% of its canvas, as photographed [3]. A blue this saturated sits outside the range most historical pigments and aged varnish can reach on a photograph, which describes our museum holdings rather than painting as a whole [3].

origin.named_after: the modifier neon + blue; the color itself traces to Werner's 1821 nomenclature
